data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Bacchus was the god of wine, fertility, and ecstasy. His name is derived from the Greek word 'basko', meaning to shout or cry out, which may refer to the ecstatic frenzy experienced during Bacchic rituals. In Christianity, Bacchus is sometimes identified with Christ and associated with the Eucharist.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bac total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: In ancient Rome, Bacchus was considered a dual god, associated not only with wine and agriculture but also with wild parties and revelry. Wine played a significant role in Roman society, and Bacchus was a symbol of the pleasures to be found in its consumption.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the spiritual significance of Bacchus is found in the Eucharist, the sacrament of the Body and Blood of Christ. Like Bacchus, Christ transforms ordinary elements (bread and wine) into something extraordinary, imparting grace and a taste of the divine.
